---
title: "Part 4 – Replication and preregistration"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/housing-one-day-open-science.html#/part-4-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 4 leaves the original file behind. After a short look at how far the answer moves when the analysis changes on those same data, it turns to the replication that SCORE ran with new emails and new names, reads the plan that was registered before the first email went out, and ends on a preregistration of your own, filled in before any result exists and not run.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, with [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) as the follow-up | The curve of the claim: the 64 specifications that the course judged justifiable on these data, ranked from the largest gap to the smallest, with the published result of the original authors (OAs) and the five analysts placed on it. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, with [the replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) on the case study as the follow-up | The SCORE replication, a preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities with new names; what it found; the original study and the replication compared row by row; the power of the two designs; the three Rs on this paper; and what separates robustness from replicability. | 16 minutes |
| Slides | The preregistration of the replication: what it fixed, what the final report added, and how a reader can tell the two apart. Then what a preregistration fixes, and what it leaves open. | 10 minutes |
| Slides, with [Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd) as the follow-up | Where a reanalysis is archived and registered, the preregistration of Multi100 itself, the two preregistration templates, the public record of the case with a three-minute search of the replication report, and the eight AsPredicted questions mapped onto the decisions of the analysis. | 14 minutes |
| [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration) Task 5, without the run | Fill in the preregistration cell: the claim, the data and what you already know about them, one option for each decision on the `my_` lines, a sentence from your estimand statement on why your choices answer the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Copy the block into your notes. Nothing is fitted and nothing is sent; if you run the cell, it only checks your choices and prints the block. Then swap with a neighbour: could they run your analysis from your block alone? | 30 minutes |
| Slides | What you take with you, and the feedback form. | 8 minutes |

**By the end of the part** you can say what a replication with new data adds to a reproduction and to a check of robustness, you can read a replication report against its preregistration, and you have a preregistration block of your own, filled in before any result existed.
